-


**Layering beats replacing:** WestCX built its orchestration platform across existing EHRs, CRMs, and CCaaS systems instead of replacing them.


-


**Keep your decision engine:** Nova Gestões integrated programmable communication into its existing stack and retained control of its core business logic.


-

## How to modernize CX without ripping and replacing your stack


30% of businesses say their[tech stacks can't keep up](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/report/navigating-data-deluge-charting-customer-context#:~:text=The%20new%20systems%20lighting%20the%20way) with customer expectations.


Naturally, they jump to replacement. We need a new platform, migration plan, 18-month roadmap, and a validation board deck. Fortunately, there’s a better (and easier) way to keep up.


The CIOs and CTOs in[Twilio's Innovators Report](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/lp/innovators-report) mostly didn't rip and replace their tech stacks. Five executives across:


1.


Healthcare


2.


Retail


3.


Financial services


4.


Lending


They all managed to modernize customer engagement while keeping the systems they already ran. Here’s how.


## Replacement is almost always the safer plan


Every platform sold to a CIO looks clean in the demo. You’ve seen them. The demo runs on tidy data and consistent processes. But your business situation is always messier (no judgement, either). You probably run on dozens of systems that disagree with each other, layered with a decade of exceptions that exist because someone needed them.


Replacement projects don’t hit that wall during the demo. They don’t even hit it during the pilot. No, you don’t violently crash into this wall until month nine, long after the budget is committed and the old system is half-decommissioned. It’s too late then.


**Layering fails differently, though.**


If the layer doesn't work, the systems underneath still do. That asymmetry is why this approach keeps showing up among executives who have been through both.


## 5 patterns from CIOs who modernized without replacing


These aren’t hypothetical situations. These are real CIOs producing real results. These are published results from the deployments:


-


[Sweetwater](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/lp/innovators-report/innovator-2) : 50,000 texts and 40,000 calls daily, 850 agents enabled, contact center setups deployed in under two days.


-


[WestCX](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/lp/innovators-report/innovator-1) : 50 to 80% higher RCS conversion rates than SMS or email, three times the customer engagement, 20% revenue uplift from reduced no-shows.


-


[Eltropy](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/lp/innovators-report/innovator-5) : up to 70% average containment across dozens of active voice deployments, with 24/7 availability for community banks that can't staff nights and weekends.


-


[Nova Gestões](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/lp/innovators-report/innovator-3) : lower first response times and reduced cost per contact after moving conversations to digital channels.


None of these results came from a platform replacement.


### 1. Put the orchestration layer above the systems of record


[WestCX consolidated billing, scheduling, and care instructions](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/lp/innovators-report/innovator-1) into a single layer through WestCX Orchestrate. The platform handles complex tasks like appointment rescheduling and insurance verification, and it knows when to escalate to a human specialist.


They made the architectural decision to layer across existing systems (including EHRs, CRMs, and CCaaS platforms) instead of replacing them. In a regulated healthcare environment, replacing the system of record isn't a realistic option, so the layer went above it.


CIO Juan Rosero's guidance is to **prioritize orchestration design, since channels change but the customer journey doesn't.**[Build an engagement layer](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/resource-center/winning-engagement-strategy) that understands context, intent, and history.


### 2. Integrate into the CRM you already have


[Sweetwater was scaling white-glove service](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/lp/innovators-report/innovator-2) through explosive growth and running into the limits of homegrown systems. They kept the CRM and integrated[Twilio Voice](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/voice) and[Messaging](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/messaging) directly into it, so sales engineers keep full context across every SMS and voice interaction.


CIO Jason Johnson's first best practice is exactly that: **centralize the customer view by integrating voice and SMS into your CRM so agents always have current context, history, and preferences.**


### 3. Keep control of your decision engine


[Nova Gestões handles millions of sensitive financial negotiations a month](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/lp/innovators-report/innovator-3) under strict regulatory control. They used mature, well-documented APIs to integrate programmable communication into their existing stacks, which let them retain full control over their core business logic and decision engines.


CTO Juliano Skrzyszowski recommends not handing your core business to third parties. **Instead,[build your own orchestration layer](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/ai-agent-orchestration) and keep your own decision engine.**


### 4. Unify the data layer before you scale AI


[Lendi Group moved from a heritage broker model](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/lp/innovators-report/innovator-4) where context lived across disconnected systems toward an architecture treating SMS, voice, and chat as one living thread.


**CTO Devesh Maheshwari advises organizations to eliminate the data fragment tax by unifying your real-time data layer before scaling AI or automation. This way, every agent, human or AI works from one source of truth.**


Data backs up this recommendation.[48% of companies name connecting data across channels as their top obstacle to understanding customers](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/report/great-ai-illusion-why-customers-value-empathy#:~:text=48%25%20of%20businesses%20struggle%20to%20understand%20their%20customers%20because%20their%20data%20is%20fragmented%20across%20channels.) , and[84% of brands say their AI can access customer history](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/report/navigating-data-deluge-charting-customer-context#:~:text=84%25%20of%20brands,their%20AI%20agents.) while only 40% design personalization around it.


Adding AI on top of fragmented data reproduces the same fragmentation at higher speeds.


### 5. Ship behind sandboxes and flags


[Sweetwater prototypes and rolls out new workflows gradually](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/lp/innovators-report/innovator-2) using sandboxes and feature flags, with automated compliance for consent and data retention built into the CRM, peer-reviewed code, and audit logs. **That governance lets them deploy new contact center configurations in under two days.**


This is the tactic you can borrow for all other recommendations. Ultimately, incremental modernization only works if you can ship small changes without a major release event.


## How to modernize your own CX


Here’s a replicable step-by-step process:


1.


**Map where context breaks.** Age isn't the problem. The seams between systems usually are.


2.


**Pick the highest-volume journey.** You need a baseline before you can show anyone a result.


3.


**Add the layer above one journey.** Keep every system of record in place.


4.


**Unify the data feeding that journey.** Do this before adding AI to it.


5.


**Prove it, then scale.** Each journey you add makes the next one cheaper.


## Modernize the seams first


The stack that can't keep pace doesn’t fail at storage or processing. It's usually failing at the handoffs, where one system knows something the next one needs but there’s no path between them.


Fortunately, those are cheaper to fix than to replace, and the five executives in the[Innovators Report](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/lp/innovators-report) have the operational numbers to back this up.

## Frequently asked questions


### Can I modernize customer experience without replacing my existing systems?


Yes. In Twilio's Innovators Report, WestCX built its orchestration platform across existing EHRs, CRMs, and CCaaS systems instead of replacing them, and Sweetwater integrated voice and messaging into its existing CRM.


### What is an orchestration layer in customer engagement?


An orchestration layer sits above your systems of record and moves context between them, handling routing, escalation, and journey logic. WestCX uses one to consolidate billing, scheduling, and care instructions without replacing those systems.


### Should I fix my data before deploying AI agents?


Yes. Lendi Group's CTO recommends unifying your real-time data layer before scaling AI. Twilio research found 84% of brands say their AI can access customer history while only 40% design personalization around it.


### How do I avoid vendor lock-in when modernizing CX?


Nova Gestões' CTO recommends keeping your own orchestration layer and decision engine, integrating through documented APIs instead of handing over core business logic. That keeps the systems you depend on under your control.


### How long does incremental CX modernization take?


It varies by journey, but Sweetwater deploys new contact center configurations in under two days using sandboxes, feature flags, and automated compliance checks built into its CRM.
